evidence.budget_forced: fixes landed for confirmed findings #1 #2 #3 #5; re-review to clear

chunk_findings.detail: `_param_end` still treats the first `}` as the end of `${...}` and never skips a quoted span, so a `)` that bash still considers part of the expansion is taken as the `$()` closer and the rest of the substitution is dropped. For `echo "$(echo ${x:-"}")}; git push origin main)"`, bash’s matching `}` is the one after the quoted `}`, the `)` before that `}` is literal text inside `${x:-...}`, and bash then runs `git push origin main` inside the substitution. `_param_end` returns at the `}` inside the quotes; `_find_body` then stops at that `)`, the body appended is only `echo ${x:-"}`, and `_dquote_end` leaves `git push` as ordinary double-quoted text, so `check` returns None. The later hunk that touches `_param_end` is not this function: the body shown here still has no quote walk.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_param_end

chunk_findings.detail: `_has_esac` still searches the raw string for a bare `esac` and ignores quotes, so a `case` word plus an `esac` that is only literal text makes `_skip_span` enter case mode and swallow the real `$()` closer. For `echo "$(echo case x); git push origin main; esac"`, bash closes the substitution at the `)` after `x` and prints the rest, including `git push`, without executing it. `_has_esac` still sees the quoted `esac`, `_case_end` walks past that `)`, and the body appended to `bodies` includes `git push origin main`, so the guard refuses a command bash never runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_has_esac

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten descent still treats `-c` as a whole word: `"-c" in head` is false and `head.index("-c")` never runs for a clustered flag. Given `bash -exc 'git push origin main'` (and `sh -xc 'git push origin main'`), bash enables `-e -x -c` and executes `git push origin main`, but the words are `['bash', '-exc', 'git push origin main']`, so the payload is never `_split` and `check` returns None. The same holds for `-exc` on the other shells in `_SHELLS`. This is the prior clustered-flag miss; this hunk does not call a flag splitter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The new hunks only change `${...}` scanning, unclosed-sub mask clamping, and `_sh_c`. They do not make `esac` quote-aware, so the earlier case still fails: given `echo "$(echo case x); git push origin main; esac"`, bash closes the substitution at the `)` after `x` and does not run `git push`, but a raw `esac` search still throws case mode past that `)`, the substitution body is kept, and `check` refuses a command bash never executes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_has_esac

chunk_findings.detail: `_sh_c` treats any short token containing `c` as the shell’s `-c` and does not stop at the first operand. Given `bash ./tool.sh -cache 'git push origin main'`, bash runs `./tool.sh` with those two arguments and does not execute `git push`; the old exact `"-c" in head` check left this alone, but `"c" in "cache"` now returns that index and `_split`s the next word, so `check` refuses a command that never runs. The same misfire hits `bash -ocpipefail 'git push origin main'`, where `-o` consumes `cpipefail` and the quoted string is the script name, not a `-c` payload.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_sh_c

data.probe: check('echo "$(echo ${x:-"}"}); git push origin main)"') returns REFUSED git push on the current tree: _param_end walks the quoted span via _dquote_end, so the quoted } is not taken for the brace's close; bash runs git push inside the substitution, and the guard sees it.
